ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

2. When practising Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.

3. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.

4. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.

5. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only a joining word

6. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.

7. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. happiness
   C. blue
   D. quickly

8. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.

9. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.

10. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. went
   C. goes
   D. goed

11. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.

12. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.

5. B — A person, place, thing, or idea

6. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.

7. A — run

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.

10. B — went

11. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.

12. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
